extracted.intended_audience: California state agencies' rulemaking staff, agency counsel, and regulatory program managers who prepare and submit Notices of Proposed Action to OAL
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for preparing and submitting a Notice of Proposed Action to the California Office of Administrative Law (OAL), including content requirements, timing/deadlines, and attachments required for publication in the California Regulatory Notice Register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Receipt deadline for publication
rubrics_metrics.description: To be published, a Notice must be received by OAL no later than 10 calendar days before the publication date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OAL publishes the Notice Register every Friday; submit at least 10 calendar days before the desired Friday issue to be included. Use the Notice Register Publication Schedule to determine the exact receipt deadline for a desired publication date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication lead time before close of comments/hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice for a rulemaking must be published at least 45 calendar days before the close of the public comment period and public hearing, if a hearing is scheduled (Government Code section 11346.4(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should plan backward from the desired close of comments/hearing to ensure the Notice is scheduled at least 45 calendar days prior; coordinate with OAL publication dates and the 10-day receipt deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: One-year rulemaking file completion requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A state agency must complete its rulemaking and submit the rulemaking file to OAL within one year of the date of publication of a Notice of Proposed Action (“Notice”) in the Notice Register. (Government Code Section 11346.4(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must track the Notice publication date as the start of the one-year period for completing the rulemaking and submitting the file to OAL; failure to meet the one-year deadline may affect processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required substantive contents of the Notice of Proposed Action
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice of Proposed Action contains a variety of information about the nature of the proposed regulatory changes including various findings, determinations, statutory authority and the law(s) being implemented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include clear findings and determinations, cite statutory authority and the specific law(s) being implemented. Also provide procedural information (see next criterion) and ensure referenced supporting documents (Express Terms, Initial Statement of Reasons) are available as indicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required procedural information in the Notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice of Proposed Action also contains procedural information, such as deadlines for submitting comments, scheduling of hearings (if any), and where copies of the Express Terms, Initial Statement of Reasons, and any other supporting information can be obtained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state the comment deadline, hearing date/time/location (if scheduled), and the means/locations for obtaining or inspecting supporting documents (e.g., office address, web links, contact information).

rubrics_metrics.name: Economic Impact Assessment inclusion for non-major regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: For non-major regulations, the results of the Economic Impact Assessment will be included in the Notice of Proposed Action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare and include the Economic Impact Assessment results when the regulation is non-major; ensure the assessment is clear and accessible in the Notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Department of Finance commentary inclusion for major regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: If the rulemaking is a major regulation, any comments provided by the Department of Finance, along with the agency’s responses, will be included in the Notice of Proposed Action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For major regulations, obtain and incorporate Dept. of Finance comments and the agency’s formal responses into the Notice materials so they will be published with the Notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference to Section 5, Title 1 CCR for required submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 5, Title 1, California Code of Regulations describes what an agency must submit with its Notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult Section 5, Title 1 CCR for the specific list of documents and formatting/filing requirements that must accompany the Notice when submitted to OAL.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of the Notice Register Publication Schedule to determine OAL receipt deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: The California Regulatory Notice Register Publication Schedule identifies the required deadline date for OAL to receive the Notice for publication in order to meet the desired date for the close of the written public comment period and for the public hearing, if a hearing is scheduled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the Publication Schedule when planning filings to ensure the Notice receipt date with OAL aligns with the agency’s desired comment-period close and hearing schedule; factor in the weekly Friday publication cycle and the 10-day receipt rule.
